stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: An economist randomly selected 400 people from the list of everyone who filed for unemployment benefits in one state during 2025. Of these 400 people, 200 were randomly assigned to attend a weekly résumé workshop, and the other 200 were given no workshop. After six months, the workshop group had a significantly higher reemployment rate than the group with no workshop.
choices: The workshop is associated with higher reemployment for these 400 people, but it cannot be said to cause it.
The workshop causes higher reemployment for people who filed for unemployment benefits in that state during 2025.
The workshop causes higher reemployment for people who file for unemployment benefits in any state in any year.
The workshop causes higher reemployment for the 400 people studied, but the result cannot be extended beyond them.
explanation: Check both kinds of randomness. People were randomly assigned to the workshop or to no workshop, so you can draw a cause-and-effect conclusion. They were also randomly selected from everyone who filed in that state during 2025, so the conclusion extends to that population and no further.

A.why: You treated this like an observational study. The workshop was randomly assigned, so the study supports a causal claim, not just an association.

C.why: You stretched the conclusion past the population sampled. The 400 people came from one state in one year, so the result cannot be generalized to every state and every year.

D.why: You ignored the random selection. Because the 400 were randomly chosen from all 2025 filers in the state, the causal conclusion extends to that whole group, not just the people studied.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: An engineer randomly selected 150 steel bridges from the inspection records of all steel bridges in one region. For each bridge, the engineer noted whether the builder had applied a zinc coating and counted the corrosion cracks found at the most recent inspection. The bridges with a zinc coating had, on average, far fewer corrosion cracks than the bridges without one.
choices: Zinc coating causes fewer corrosion cracks in steel bridges in the region.
Zinc coating causes fewer corrosion cracks in steel bridges everywhere.
Zinc coating is associated with fewer corrosion cracks only in the 150 bridges.
Zinc coating is associated with fewer corrosion cracks in the region's bridges.
explanation: The engineer only recorded which bridges already had a coating. Nothing was randomly assigned, so you can claim an association but not a cause. The bridges were randomly selected from all steel bridges in the region, so the association extends to the region's steel bridges.

A.why: You accepted a causal claim from observational data. The engineer did not decide which bridges got a coating, so other differences between the bridges could explain the cracks.

B.why: You made two mistakes: you claimed a cause from an observational study, and you generalized beyond the region the bridges were sampled from.

C.why: You overlooked the random selection. Because the 150 bridges were randomly drawn from all steel bridges in the region, the association can be extended to that whole population.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: An agronomist asked farmers to volunteer fields for a soil study, and 60 farmers each volunteered one field. The agronomist randomly assigned 30 of the fields to be treated with biochar and left the other 30 untreated. At harvest, the treated fields produced a significantly higher average wheat yield than the untreated fields.
choices: Biochar causes higher wheat yields on fields like those in the study, but not necessarily on all farms.
Biochar is associated with higher wheat yields on these fields, but the study cannot show that it causes them.
Biochar causes higher wheat yields on all farms, because the fields were randomly assigned to treatments.
Biochar is associated with higher wheat yields on all farms, but the study cannot show that it causes them.
explanation: The fields were randomly assigned to biochar or no biochar, so you can conclude that biochar caused the higher yields. The fields were volunteered rather than randomly selected, so the conclusion applies only to fields like those in the study.

B.why: You mixed up the two kinds of randomness. Without random selection you can't generalize as far, but you still get the causal claim that random assignment allows.

C.why: You used random assignment to justify generalizing. Random assignment supports cause, but only random selection lets you extend the result to all farms, and these fields were volunteered.

D.why: You got both parts backward. You denied the cause that random assignment supports, and you generalized to all farms when the fields were never randomly selected.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A county newspaper asked residents with private wells to mail in water samples, and 80 well owners did so. A hydrologist tested the samples and found that wells located within 1 kilometer of an irrigation canal had higher average nitrate levels than wells located farther away.
choices: Being near a canal causes higher nitrate levels in the wells that were tested.
Being near a canal is associated with higher nitrate levels in all county wells.
Being near a canal is associated with higher nitrate levels in the tested wells.
Being near a canal causes higher nitrate levels in all private wells in the county.
explanation: No one assigned wells to be near or far from a canal, so you can only claim an association. The well owners chose to send samples rather than being randomly selected, so the association applies only to the wells that were tested.

A.why: You read a causal claim into observational data. Wells near canals may differ in other ways, such as being near farmland, so the study cannot show that distance from a canal is the cause.

B.why: You generalized from a self-selected group. Owners who chose to mail in samples were not randomly selected, so the result cannot be extended to all county wells.

D.why: You made both errors at once. You claimed a cause without random assignment, and you generalized to the county without random selection.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A city planning office randomly selected 500 households from a list of all residential addresses in the city. Each household reported how many days per week its members commute by bicycle. Households located within 400 meters of a protected bike lane reported significantly more bicycle commuting days, on average, than households located farther away.
choices: Living near a bike lane causes more bicycle commuting for households in the city.
Living near a bike lane is associated with more bicycle commuting only for the 500 households.
Living near a bike lane is associated with more bicycle commuting for households in the city.
Living near a bike lane causes more bicycle commuting for households in cities in general.
explanation: Households chose where to live, so nothing was randomly assigned and you can claim only an association. The 500 households were randomly selected from all residential addresses in the city, so the association can be generalized to households in the city.

A.why: You treated a strong association as a cause. People who already like cycling may choose to live near bike lanes, so the survey cannot show that the lanes caused the commuting.

B.why: You ignored the random selection. Because the households were randomly chosen from every address in the city, the association extends to the whole city.

D.why: You claimed a cause without random assignment, and you generalized to other cities when the sample came from only one city.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Researchers randomly selected 300 patients aged 65 or older from the registry of a hospital network. Half of these patients were randomly assigned to receive a high-dose flu vaccine, and the other half received the standard dose. One month later, the high-dose group had significantly higher average antibody levels than the standard-dose group.
choices: The high dose causes higher antibody levels for the network's patients aged 65 or older.
The high dose causes higher antibody levels for the network's patients of every age group.
The high dose is associated with higher antibody levels, but it cannot be said to cause them.
The high dose causes higher antibody levels for the 300 patients studied and for no one else.
explanation: The dose was randomly assigned, so you can conclude cause and effect. The patients were randomly selected from the network's patients aged 65 or older, so the conclusion applies to that group.

B.why: You generalized past the population that was sampled. Only patients aged 65 or older were selected, so the result says nothing about younger patients.

C.why: You treated this experiment like an observational study. Randomly assigning the dose is exactly what allows a causal conclusion.

D.why: You overlooked the random selection. The 300 patients were randomly drawn from the network's older patients, so the conclusion extends to that whole group.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A coach recruited 40 college swimmers who volunteered for a training study. Twenty of the swimmers were randomly assigned to follow a two-week tapering plan before a meet, and the other 20 kept their usual training. At the meet, the tapering group improved their 100-meter times by significantly more, on average, than the other group.
choices: The tapering plan causes greater improvement for all college swimmers.
The tapering plan is associated with greater improvement for all college swimmers.
The tapering plan is associated with greater improvement for the swimmers studied.
The tapering plan causes greater improvement for swimmers like those studied.
explanation: The swimmers were randomly assigned to tapering or usual training, so you can conclude that the plan caused the greater improvement. They volunteered rather than being randomly selected, so the conclusion is limited to swimmers like those in the study.

A.why: You generalized from volunteers to all college swimmers. Without random selection, the result cannot be extended to the whole population.

B.why: You swapped the roles of the two kinds of randomness. You downgraded the cause that random assignment supports, and you generalized without random selection.

C.why: You stopped at association even though the plan was randomly assigned. Random assignment is what allows a cause-and-effect conclusion.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A meteorologist randomly selected 120 summer days from the records of a single coastal weather station covering 1995 through 2024. For each day, the meteorologist recorded the morning wind direction and whether rain fell that afternoon. Afternoon rain was recorded significantly more often on days with an easterly morning wind than on other days.
choices: An easterly morning wind causes afternoon rain on summer days at that station.
An easterly morning wind is associated with afternoon rain on summer days at that station.
An easterly morning wind is associated with afternoon rain on summer days at any station.
An easterly morning wind causes afternoon rain on summer days at coastal stations generally.
explanation: The meteorologist only recorded the weather that happened. No wind direction was assigned, so you can claim only an association. The days were randomly selected from that station's summer records, so the association applies to summer days at that station.

A.why: You accepted a cause from observational records. Other conditions that come with easterly winds, such as moist air from the sea, could explain the rain.

C.why: You generalized beyond the population sampled. Every day came from one station, so the association cannot be extended to other stations.

D.why: You made both errors. You claimed a cause without random assignment, and you extended the result to other stations that were never sampled.
